research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: How is 'reorganization relative to L' operationalised, and is L a baseline fingerprint, a leave-one-out quantity, or something else?
Is the regression of PPP change on reorganization estimated at the spell level (148 spells) or at the player-season level (n=986)?
What minimum detectable correlation do 148 spells give, and is that adequate for the expected effect?
How are regression to the mean, usage and lineup-quality confounding, and selection into absence handled?
Do placebo or null-model checks rule out artifacts of the construction, as the retrieved audit requires?

historical_evidence.finding: Records that connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence: unmatched connector vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021 (t=5.97, p=2.87e-08); usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96; vs terminal +0.0777, t=2.37, p=0.0261, n=25. Sample 908 player-seasons. Limited by small_sample; carries MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks.

Records that real on/off absence of a shaper displaces the team fingerprint more than a usage-matched non-shaper: delta D_A=+0.115 (t=6.35, p~7e-9; shaper larger in 81% of pairs); delta D_pi=+0.011 (p~1e-4); r(L,D_A)=+0.60 (shapers +0.79). Built on 908 player-seasons with >=400 possessions on and off, and 96 usage-matched pairs (caliper 0.03). Validation recorded as no_validation_recorded.

Tail/null-model audit of a published suppression excess: reproduced excess 0.4080 (CI [0.378,0.438]), but the within-unit permutation null gives 0.3744 (residual +0.0054, z 0.40); asymmetry neg-pos 0.0176 (p=0.258); drift-centred tail mass ratio 1.007. Recorded failure mechanism C_artifact. Limited by drift, insufficient exposure and selection or regression to the mean.

Superstar sequential suppression: PUTBACK is the top opponent-prior play type suppressing next-possession PPP for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345, n=32; C. Holmgren d=-0.222, n=52). Mechanism recorded as E_unclear. No multiplicity correction; n_after 32-95 in several PUTBACK cells. No validation recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating the published suppression excess (trigger drop minus matched control drop) as a real effect without null-model and tail checks.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact (C_artifact): the excess is reproduced at 0.408 but falls to the within-unit permutation null (residual +0.0054, z 0.40), with no significant asymmetry (p=0.258). Recorded limitations: drift, insufficient exposure, selection or regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Per-star, per-play-type PPP suppression screening across 30 stars without a formal hypothesis test.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with no multiplicity correction and small post-event cells (n_after 30-95), so the ranked suppressors are not established as effects.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF-PAP-014) found that on/off absence of an organiser or shaper displaces the team offensive fingerprint D_A more than usage-matched absence, with a reported correlation of L with D_A of +0.60 in FAM:SF-PAP-014.
The 'L' baseline appears in the project's prior work as a leave-one-out fingerprint measure tied to D_A, not as a PPP quantity.
A prior suppression-excess claim did not survive a null-model audit (FAM:SF-TMP-012), so construction artifacts are a live risk in this project's data.
Per-play-type PPP results from prior work (FAM:SF-APPA-050) were exploratory with unclear mechanism.
evidence_does_not_establish: Any direct link between reorganization relative to L and change in PPP; the retrieved supported families test identity displacement D_A, not PPP change.
The effect size, sign or spell-level distribution of the reorganization-to-PPP association.
Whether the 96-pair or 908-player-season results transfer to 148 absence spells or to the 2025-26 seasons.
Whether D_A and PPP change share the same possession base, which could create mechanical correlation.
Anything about the 986-unit count, since the retrieval gives no mapping from 986 units to the 148 spells.
own_inferences: Under a two-sided alpha of 0.05 and 80% power, a Fisher-z correlation test with n=148 has an MDE of about rho=0.23. That is the usable power limit for a single pre-specified correlation; a correlation estimated on 986 units would have a smaller MDE, but those units are likely not independent.
Because the retrieved on/off families were supported only at roughly 96 usage-matched pairs and were not validated, a PPP effect of similar size would likely be borderline at 148 spells.

The question as posed is underspecified: 'relative to L' needs a fixed formula, and the outcome 'change in PPP' needs a fixed window (for example pre-absence vs during-absence PPP for the same offence).

Any reorganization measure computed from the same play-by-play as PPP change risks OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL and mechanical coupling, so the measure should be built from lineup/play-type mix and checked for independence from the outcome.
uncertainties: The retrieved records do not report a PPP-on-reorganization result for this question; the closest records concern D_A and per-star PPP suppression.
The definition of L and the reorganization measure used in the retrieved records are not fully stated.
Validation status is no_validation_recorded for the supporting families.
Data status on 2026-11-01: 2022-23 to 2024-25 and the 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are complete per the task, so the data should be fixed to a snapshot to avoid drift.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved evidence showed that the project's prior supported results concern D_A displacement, not PPP change, so the question is not already answered. It also showed a prior suppression claim failing a null-model audit (artifact) and an unvalidated PPP screen without multiplicity correction. Both raise the bar for the test. This moved the decision from a straightforward proceed to proceed_with_changes, with a pre-specified L, a placebo/null-model audit and multiplicity control required before any claim.

blocking_constraints.text: 148 spells give an MDE of about rho=0.23 for a single correlation; a smaller true effect would be missed.
Absence spells are selected on injury or rest, and PPP change is subject to regression to the mean, so raw change scores are biased.
If reorganization and PPP change are derived from the same possessions, the association may be mechanical.

prior_work.summary: Prior project work supports a connector/shaper absence effect on team identity displacement D_A (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF-PAP-014), with r(L,D_A)=+0.60 reported. It does not test reorganization relative to L against PPP change. A suppression-excess claim was an artifact on null-model audit (FAM:SF-TMP-012), and per-star PPP screening was exploratory (FAM:SF-APPA-050).

risks.text: 148 spells give an MDE around rho=0.23; the prior supported results rested on 96 pairs.
Absence is endogenous to injury and rest; PPP change regresses to the mean.
Usage, minutes, lineup quality, opponent strength and play-type mix can drive both reorganization and PPP change.
Reorganization built from the same possessions as the PPP outcome may create mechanical correlation.
Using post-absence information to define the baseline L or the reorganization measure would leak the outcome.
Flagged on the supporting families; the reorganization measure may have a floor effect that inflates or deflates the association.
Per-play-type PPP cells have small n_after (30-95), as in FAM:SF-APPA-050.
Screening over play types, players or reorganization definitions without correction inflates false positives (FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Results must survive placebo absences and shuffled spells, as the FAM:SF-TMP-012 audit showed.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons with changing rules and pace may shift PPP baselines.
The reorganization measure relative to L may be noisy at spell level, attenuating any association.

design.estimand: Partial association (slope and correlation, with CI) between standardised reorganization relative to the pre-specified baseline L and the change in offensive PPP across the absence window, adjusted for usage, minutes, lineup quality and opponent strength.
design.unit: Absence spell (one team-offence per spell), with player-season aggregation only as a sensitivity analysis.
design.sample: Up to 148 spells from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular and playoff data, with the 986 units treated as a sensitivity set and not as independent observations; fixed data snapshot dated at 2026-11-01.
design.power: At alpha=0.05 two-sided and 80% power, MDE is about rho=0.23 for n=148; report the achieved MDE and the CI width, and treat effects smaller than this as not detectable.
design.controls: Pre-specify L before outcome computation (no post-absence data). Include usage-matched controls (caliper), minutes, lineup quality, opponent strength, play-type mix, and regression-to-the-mean adjustment using pre-absence PPP trend. Keep the reorganization measure independent of the outcome possessions where possible.
design.falsification: Placebo absences (non-absence windows of matched players), shuffled spell labels, and a pre-period reorganization test; the effect must be absent in placebo and survive the FAM:SF-TMP-012-style null-model audit.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary contrast; secondary play-type and player analyses corrected (e.g. Holm or BH), and the screening structure of FAM:SF-APPA-050 is not used as confirmatory evidence.
design.decision_rule: Claim support only if the primary slope CI excludes zero, the effect exceeds the placebo distribution, and it survives the usage-matched and regression-to-the-mean controls; otherwise report inconclusive, or rejected if the CI is tight around zero at the stated MDE.
design.data_version: Fixed snapshot: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21), frozen at 2026-11-01.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: Does offensive reorganization after player absence predict the change in points per possession?
How should reorganization be measured relative to baseline L, and how sensitive is the estimate to that choice?
What sample size and minimum detectable effect are needed given the reported units (n=986; n=148 spells)?
What confounders, selection effects, and leakage risks affect spell-level tests of absence and offensive change?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
